--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.maximum_weight_clique()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Find a clique with the largest total node weight. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.maximum_weight_clique()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Find a clique with the largest total node weight. title: >- [Graph.maximum_weight_clique()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Find a clique with the largest total node weight. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a clique with the largest total node weight. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L34469-L34589){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.maximum_weight_clique(node_weight_attr=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Maximum weight clique](../assets/graphs/maximum-weight-clique.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Four nodes with weights w in badges: A 1, B 2, C 1, D 5. The triangle A, B, C has the most nodes but weighs only 1 + 2 + 1 = 4; the edge B to D, in the accent color, weighs 2 + 5 = 7. The card shows the result [B, D] with weight 7." width="100%"} With node weights (values, scores, sizes), the maximum-weight clique is the most valuable group of mutually connected nodes: the highest-scoring set of compatible features, the most valuable group of mutually compatible items or people, or the best consistent set of matches in structure alignment. Without weights it is a maximum clique, like `maximum_clique()`. Parallel edges count once and self-loops are ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_weight_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of a node attribute holding non-negative weights. If `None` (default), every node weighs 1. Every node must have the attribute. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[int], int | float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The clique's node IDs (sorted) and its total weight (`int` when unweighted). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, or a weight is missing, negative or not a number. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Branch and bound: candidates are colored greedily (heaviest first), and since a clique uses at most one node of each color class, the sum of the heaviest weight in each class bounds what the candidates can add (in the spirit of Kumlander, 2004, and Tavares et al.). The problem is NP-hard, but the bound prunes well on sparse graphs. The weight found matches NetworkX's `max_weight_clique`. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~maximum_clique`) : The clique with the most nodes. [](`~find_cliques`) : List all maximal cliques. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The triangle `A`, `B`, `C` has the most nodes, but weighs 1 + 2 + 1 = 4. The edge `B`-`D` weighs 2 + 5 = 7, and is the heaviest clique: ::: {#5f013993 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("B", "D")] ) graph.set_node_attrs("w", {"A": 1, "B": 2, "C": 1, "D": 5}) nodes, weight = graph.maximum_weight_clique(node_weight_attr="w") [graph.get_label_from_id(n) for n in nodes], weight ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (['B', 'D'], 7) ``` ::: ::: ### The most populous group of towns `towns()` holds 12 towns of a made-up county and the 26 roads between them. Two groups of four towns are all joined to one another by direct roads. `maximum_clique()` returns the one around Kestrel Bay. Weighted by population, the group around Calder, the county's largest town, wins with 83,200 people: ::: {#c07abdd6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} towns = ec.towns() label = towns.get_label_from_id largest = towns.maximum_clique() heaviest, people = towns.maximum_weight_clique("population") [label(n) for n in largest], [label(n) for n in heaviest], people ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (['Greyford', 'Halston', 'Kestrel Bay', 'Larkhill'], ['Calder', 'Elmwick', 'Fenmoor', 'Greyford'], 83200) ``` ::: ::: The largest clique (left) has 48,100 people: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#ff519130 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} from itertools import combinations towns.plot( layout="pos", highlight=list(combinations(largest, 2)), size_by="population", label_by="label", width=320, height=360, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
